cards.speaker: James
cards.text: I'd rather we craft 30% of the {calc} made in London. We're on {share}%. The Guild still sets the standard for a good piece. The more we make, the more buyers set ours beside theirs. I'm not worried about that comparison.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Let's craft 30% of London's {calc}. Our share is {share}%, and {rival} makes the most besides us. Buyers can only judge our work if they see plenty of it. More of it on the market means more of them comparing it with the Guild's.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: Aim for 30% of the {calc} crafted in London. You're on {share}%. Raw ore sells on price alone, and I don't like that. Crafted {calc} sells on quality, which is where we beat the Guild, so I want more of it out there.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: The target is 30% of London's crafted {calc}. At present it's {share}%. The Guild's work is the standard buyers know. Every piece of ours they see is a chance to show we're better, and {rival} isn't taking that chance.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: I want 30% of the {calc} crafted in London to be ours. We're on {share}%. Every piece we finish is one fewer sold raw to someone who'll make it badly. Buyers pay more for good work, and they come back for it.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: Crafting takes days, James. Raw {calc} sells this week and pays the rent this week. A pile of unfinished pieces pays nothing.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: It does take days. A finished piece sells for more than the raw {calc} does, so the wait pays for itself. The rent will still get paid.
